actor: US Bureau of Industry and Security
title: Licences required for advanced AI chips to four ASEAN countries
summary: An interim final rule, effective 19 November 2026, requires export licences for advanced chips and servers shipped to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia (reports also name Brazil), as places with an "unacceptable risk of diversion". Existing data centres providing such services have 90 days to obtain authorisation, and there are global controls on computing access above 12 million aggregate TPP for designated entities, including Chinese companies.

title: Singapore engages US authorities on the new rule
summary: Singapore defended its standing as a trusted business hub, and said it was engaging US authorities to review the details of the new measure.

title: Malaysia says data centres must comply with US AI chip rules
summary: Malaysia said data centres must comply with the US rules, and is investigating the local unit of a Singapore-based cloud computing firm that faces a US probe into whether it was used to get around export controls. An investigation is not a finding of wrongdoing.

title: Fifth person charged in an AI server fraud case
summary: Singapore charged a fifth person in relation to an AI server fraud case. Charges are allegations until a court decides.

actor: Ministry of Investment Trade and Industry (MITI)
title: Strategic Trade Permit for US-origin high-performance AI chips
summary: A mandatory permit for the export, transshipment and transit of high-performance US-origin AI chips, with advance notification where misuse or diversion is suspected.

title: Customs stop a US$13 million AI chip smuggling attempt
summary: Malaysian customs foiled an attempt to smuggle AI chips worth about US$13 million. The exact date is still to be confirmed from the customs department's own statement.

actor: US Bureau of Industry and Security
title: AI Diffusion Rule introduced (short-lived)
summary: A rule introduced in January 2025 to control the spread of advanced AI chips worldwide. It proved short-lived, and data centre investment in Southeast Asia surged by July 2025.

title: 200 MW of new data centre capacity allocated to four operators
summary: Singapore provisionally allocated 50 MW each to Digital Realty, Equinix, Keppel Data Centres and ST Telemedia Global Data Centres, on Jurong Island, through its second Data Centre Call for Application, the main way new capacity is allocated. Criteria include a power usage effectiveness of 1.25 at full IT load. The agencies will review the need for another call in 18 to 24 months.
